title: Why landslides happen
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: Why does heavy rain cause landslides?

explain.say: On any slope, gravity pulls soil and rock down. Part of that pull drags them down the slope, while friction and roots grip them in place.
As long as the grip is stronger than the downhill pull, the slope stays put. A landslide happens when the downhill pull wins.
Heavy rain is the most common trigger. Water fills the gaps between soil grains, adding weight and pushing the grains apart, so friction gets much weaker.
Earthquakes can shake slopes loose, and people can make slopes weaker by cutting into them or removing trees whose roots held the soil together.

faq.a: Gravity pulls rock and soil down slopes. A landslide happens when something makes the slope weaker or heavier, like heavy rain, an earthquake, erosion at the bottom, or cutting down trees.

faq.q: Why does heavy rain cause landslides?
faq.a: Rainwater soaks into the ground, making it heavier, and the water pressure pushes soil grains apart so they grip each other less. The slope can then slide like wet sand.
asks: How does rain make a mudslide?

faq.a: By planting trees and shrubs whose roots bind soil, draining water out of slopes, building retaining walls and nets, and avoiding building on unstable slopes.

faq.q: What is the difference between a landslide and a rockfall?
faq.a: In a rockfall, pieces of rock break off a cliff and fall freely. In a landslide, a mass of soil and rock slides down a slope together. Mudflows are wet, runny landslides.
Yes. Shaking loosens soil and rock and can set off thousands of landslides at once in hilly places. These can be more deadly than the shaking itself.

facts: Heavy or long-lasting rainfall is the most common trigger of landslides.
Plant roots help bind soil and make slopes more stable.

quiz.say: Why can cutting down trees on a hillside make landslides more likely?
quiz.show: Removing trees makes slopes weaker because…

options.show: Roots no longer hold the soil together
options.say: Roots no longer hold the soil together

quiz.why: Tree roots bind soil and soak up water; without them the soil grips less and gets wetter.

wrong.1: Trees have no effect on earthquakes.
wrong.2: Trees do not change the steepness of a slope.
